> AGENT

Need to check what HA actually sees. Run inside your devcontainer (where HA is running):

```
ls -la /config/custom_components/lock_code_manager/www/generated/lock-code-manager.js
curl -I http://localhost:8123/lock_code_manager_files/generated/lock-code-manager.js
grep -E "Exposed strategy|lock_code_manager_files" /config/home-assistant.log | tail -10
```

What I'm checking:

1. **Does HA's view of the file exist?** If `ls` returns "No such file" but the workspace file exists, HA's `custom_components/lock_code_manager/` is a separate copy / broken symlink, not the workspace's.
2. **What does the URL actually return?** `curl -I` will show 200/404 plus headers (and the path it tried).
3. **What did HA log on startup?** The integration logs `Exposed strategy module at /lock_code_manager_files/generated/lock-code-manager.js` — if that line is missing, `async_setup` didn't run; if it's present, the static path was registered.

Most likely culprit: the devcontainer mounts a separate `/config` and `custom_components/` is symlinked. After you switched branches, the symlink may be pointing at the right path but the file content didn't propagate, or HA was started before the symlink was set up. The three commands above will pinpoint which.

> AGENT

That's the answer. PINs are crossed out (`text-decoration: line-through`) when the `.lcm-code.disabled` class is applied — which happens for slots where:

- The lock currently has **no PIN** on it (empty/null `slot.code`)
- BUT the LCM slot has a `configured_code` or `configured_code_length` in its config

So the cross-out means: **"this slot is configured with a PIN, but the lock doesn't currently have it"** — typically because the LCM slot is disabled (Enable toggle off) or otherwise blocked, so the code hasn't been pushed/has been removed from the lock.

The visual semantics: "there's a PIN here in theory, but it's not active on the lock." A user sees the masked dots (so they know a PIN is configured) with a strikethrough (so they know it's not currently usable).

Logic is in `_getCodeClass` at `ts/lock-codes-card.ts:609-625`. Style is in `lcmCodeStyles` at `ts/shared-styles.ts:150-153`. This is pre-existing behavior, not introduced by Phase 2.

Want any change to it (e.g., different visual cue, or only strike when explicitly disabled vs blocked)?

> DEVELOPER

I wonder if it should get some other type of treatment. What would a designer recommend

> AGENT

Strikethrough is semantically wrong — it means "deleted/invalid" but the PIN is just **not currently on the lock**. It also looks broken on `••••` dots (the strike doesn't have proper characters to bisect).

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The state being represented is actually two states collapsed into one: **(a) intentionally off** (slot's Enable toggle is off — PIN exists in config but admin disabled it) vs **(b) pending sync** (slot is enabled but the lock hasn't received the code yet, e.g., during a sync error or before first push). Treating them identically loses information the user needs to act on.
- HA's design language for "not currently active but exists" is usually heavy dimming + a status hint (icon or word). It almost never uses strikethrough — that's reserved for things like deleted Lovelace cards or toggled-off automations in the trace UI.
- The lock-codes-card already has the data to disambiguate (`slot.enabled === false` vs sync status). Currently it doesn't use it; the strikethrough is a single visual for both cases.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**My recommendation:**

Drop the strikethrough. Replace with two distinct treatments based on cause:

- **Intentionally off** (slot disabled by user): show `••••` in `--disabled-text-color` (heavily dimmed) with a subtle muted-background pill. No strikethrough. The visual reads as "exists but turned off" rather than "removed."
- **Pending sync / out-of-sync**: show `••••` in `--secondary-text-color` with a small `⏱` (clock) prefix or the existing sync-pending icon. Communicates "in progress" without negativity.

Both fall back gracefully if the data doesn't tell you which case applies — default to the "off" treatment.

If you want the lightest-touch fix without the disambiguation: just remove the `text-decoration: line-through` and lean on color contrast alone. The dim secondary text already reads as "not the active code." That's a 1-line change you could ship today; the disambiguation can be a follow-up.

Want me to implement the lightest version (drop the strikethrough, keep the dim color)?

> DEVELOPER

**What changed:**
- `ts/lock-codes-card.ts` — In `_renderSlotChip`, computed `isPending` mirroring `_getCodeClass` (`hasConfiguredCode && !lockHasCode && slot.enabled !== false`), added `pending` as an extra modifier on the chip's class list (alongside the existing `active`/`inactive`/`disabled` `stateClass`), and wrapped the existing `<span class="slot-name">` in a new `<span class="slot-name-row">` container that conditionally emits a `<ha-svg-icon class="slot-name-pending-icon" .path=${mdiClockOutline}>` prefix when pending. `mdiClockOutline` was already imported.
- `ts/lock-codes-card.styles.ts` — Replaced the strikethrough rule on `.slot-chip.disabled .slot-name` with a muted-pill treatment (matches `.lcm-code.off`), added `.slot-chip.pending .slot-name-pending-icon` (12px icon, secondary color, flex-shrink) and `.slot-chip.pending .slot-name` (secondary color), and added a `.slot-name-row` flex container (`align-items: center; display: inline-flex; gap: 4px`) to lay out the icon next to the name. Used `gap` on the row instead of `margin-right: 4px` on the icon, per the note in the spec.
- `ts/lock-codes-card.integration.test.ts` — Added a new `_renderSlotChip pending state on slot name` describe block with 5 tests covering the chip-class modifier, the icon-prefix presence, and the disabled vs. enabled vs. lock-has-code matrix.
- `custom_components/lock_code_manager/www/generated/lock-code-manager.js` — Regenerated bundle.

**Notable detail on the test helper:** the existing `collectAllStrings` helper only walked nested templates, not interpolated string values, so chip-class modifiers (`pending`, `disabled`, etc.) — which are pushed as plain string values into `tmpl.values` — were dropped. I extended it to also collect string values, then added a `tokenize()` helper that splits on whitespace so we can assert on `pending` as its own token without colliding with the hyphenated `slot-name-pending-icon` class.

**Layout concern (per the spec's request):** Wrapping the name in a flex `slot-name-row` keeps the icon and name aligned to each other, but the icon prefix WILL push the name itself ~16px to the right (12px icon + 4px gap) on pending slots compared to non-pending slots in the same column. Sibling rows without the icon will have their names left-aligned to the chip edge while pending rows will appear indented. Given the icon is small and the chips are visually distinct cards (not a strict tabular layout), this is consistent with the PIN's pending icon treatment and shouldn't be jarring — but if you want strict left-alignment across all chip names, the icon would need to be absolutely positioned or rendered into a fixed-width gutter. The current approach matches the PR spec verbatim.

should the name get a title NAME?

> DEVELOPER

should the name get a title NAME, everything else on the card seems to

> AGENT

No — the name is the **identity** of the slot, not a labeled field. Other elements get labels because they're values within a context (PIN belongs to the slot; CONDITIONS lists what gates the slot; LOCK STATUS shows where the slot is synced). Their labels disambiguate "which thing am I looking at?"

The name has no such ambiguity. It's the title of the card. Adding `NAME` above "test" would be like writing `TITLE: My Document` at the top of a Word doc — the position and prominence already communicate what it is. Compare with the kicker (`SLOT 10 · TEST`): that's not a label for the name, it's secondary context (which slot, which integration).

If anything, the issue is the *name lacks an obvious "this is editable" affordance* — the pencil button is the cue. If you want the field to feel more like a labeled property (consistent with PIN), the right move would be to demote the name out of the title position entirely and put it inside the hero row alongside PIN:

```
NAME      test ✎
PIN       ••••  👁              Enabled ●
```

That would make all editable fields visually parallel. Trade-off: the card loses the personable "this is Alice's slot" identity at the top, becoming more form-like.

The current design (name as title, others as labeled fields) is the more common pattern for entity-like cards in HA. I'd leave it. But if the asymmetry bothers you, the form-like layout above is the consistent alternative.

455	        // Pending: slot has a configured code but the lock doesn't have it yet.
456	        // Mirrors the .lcm-code.pending detection on the PIN — out-of-sync,
457	        // syncing, etc. Defensive default when enabled is unknown (undefined
458	        // doesn't mean "off").
459	        const lockHasCode = !isSlotEmpty(slot.code) || !!slot.code_length;
460	        const isPending = hasConfiguredCode && !lockHasCode && slot.enabled !== false;
461	
462	        // Determine state for LCM-managed slots:
463	        // - Active: active=true (code on lock, conditions met)
464	        // - Inactive: enabled=true + active=false (enabled but conditions blocking)
465	        // - Disabled: enabled=false (user explicitly disabled)
466	        // - Empty: no code and no configured_code (unmanaged empty slot)
467	        let stateClass: string;
468	        let statusText: string;
469	        let statusClass: string;

471	        if (slot.active === true) {
472	            // Binary sensor ON = active (code on lock, conditions met)
473	            stateClass = 'active';
474	            statusText = 'Active';
475	            statusClass = 'active';
476	        } else if (slot.enabled === true && slot.active === false) {
477	            // Enabled switch ON but binary sensor OFF = inactive (conditions blocking)
478	            stateClass = 'inactive';
479	            statusText = 'Inactive';
480	            statusClass = 'inactive';
481	        } else if (slot.enabled === false) {
482	            // Enabled switch OFF = disabled by user
483	            stateClass = 'disabled';
484	            statusText = 'Disabled';
485	            statusClass = 'disabled';
486	        } else if (hasCode) {
487	            // Fallback: has code on lock but no LCM state info
488	            stateClass = 'active';
489	            statusText = 'Active';
490	            statusClass = 'active';
491	        } else if (hasConfiguredCode) {
492	            // Fallback: has configured code but unknown state
493	            stateClass = 'inactive';
494	            statusText = 'Inactive';
495	            statusClass = 'inactive';
496	        } else {

634	        const mode = this._config?.code_display ?? DEFAULT_CODE_DISPLAY;

638	        if (slot.code === SLOT_CODE_UNREADABLE || slot.code_length) return 'masked';

645	        if (slot.configured_code || slot.configured_code_length) {
646	            const cause = slot.enabled === false ? 'off' : 'pending';
647	            return `${cause}${maskSuffix}`;
648	        }
649	        return 'no-code';

> DEVELOPER

as a designer, how would you reduce the vertical size of the slots in the lock card while maintaining fidelity of information?

> AGENT

The lock card shows N slots at once — the labels that work on the slot card (one focused slot) become repetitive noise here. Same `NAME` and `PIN` text on every chip is information the user has to filter past on every glance.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Labels disambiguate fields where the user might be uncertain what they're looking at. On a multi-slot list, position and typography do that job better than text — the user sees "rows of slots" once and the pattern is set; repeating "NAME" / "PIN" on every chip is noise.
- The visual parallelism with the slot card doesn't require literal labels — it requires consistent treatment. Name = bold primary text, PIN = monospace dots. Those typographic conventions are recognized without needing to be named.
- Lock cards typically expand vertically with the number of slots; reducing per-chip height has compounding effect. Saving 20px per slot saves 200px on a 10-slot lock.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**My recommendation:** drop the NAME/PIN labels on the lock card; let position and typography carry the meaning. Keep the labels on the slot card (one focused slot — labels are useful context).

The layout becomes two rows per chip:

```
Slot 5 · House Locks                    [Active] [Managed]
Alice                              ••••  👁
```

Saves ~30-40% vertical space per chip. All the same information; nothing hidden.

If you want even tighter, the most aggressive move is **single-line per chip**:

```
[5]  Alice · House Locks · Active · Managed       ••••  👁
```

But that breaks the chip-as-card visual language and starts feeling table-like. The two-row version preserves the chip feel while still being substantially tighter.

Want me to apply the two-row version?

> DEVELOPER

I wonder, is there any value in having the condition be collapsed if the condition is applied? What would you tell me as a designer?

> AGENT

There's value in collapsing when the condition is **passing** (Active state). The user opening the card already saw `✓ Vacation calendar` in the summary badge — that's all the confirmation they need. Expanding by default just adds visual weight to a "things are fine" state.

But when the condition is **blocking** (Inactive state), the user is almost certainly opening the card to figure out *why* their PIN doesn't work. Hiding the cause behind a click is friction at exactly the moment they need it.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The principle is "show what matters when it matters". The condition section's value isn't constant — it's high-value when blocking, low-value when passing. Defaulting to expanded-when-blocking matches that asymmetry.
- This is a standard dashboard pattern (e.g., HA's notification panel auto-expands errors but stays compact for info). It's not surprising once users see it once.
- The user can still toggle either direction manually — auto-expand sets the default, doesn't lock it.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**My recommendation:** auto-expand the Condition section by default when the condition is blocking (slot Inactive). Keep collapsed by default when passing (slot Active) or when slot is Disabled (condition is irrelevant if the slot is off entirely).

The empty state (no condition) stays as the static non-expanding row we already have.

This is a one-line change in `setConfig` or `_renderConditionsSection` — just compute initial expansion based on `active === false`. Want me to apply it?

All three reviews complete. Aggregating into a consolidated action plan.

## Aggregated review findings — PR #1116

### CRITICAL (must fix before merge)

**Accessibility (8) — keyboard-blocked interactions:**
1. **Hero PIN value** click-only `<span>`, no keyboard access (`slot-card.ts:532-539`)
2. **Hero name value** click-only span — redundant with pencil but breaks the keyboard-tab path (`slot-card.ts:503-510`)
3. **Lock-card slot chip** click-only `<div>` for managed slots, navigates with no keyboard path (`lock-codes-card.ts:507-514`)
4. **Lock-name navigation** in slot card, click-only (`slot-card.ts:916-922`)
5. **Collapsible header** click-only `<div>`, no `aria-expanded` (`shared-styles.ts:260-271`)
6. **Action error banner** missing `role="alert"` / `aria-live`
7. **"Saving…" indicator** missing `aria-live`
8. **Reveal button on managed clickable chip** doesn't `stopPropagation` — clicking eye also navigates away

**Design (4):**
1. **Hierarchy inversion**: PIN (22px monospace) dominates the name (16px small-caps) in the hero. The name should be the card's identity anchor.
2. **`Slot N · {entry_title}` is rendered at 18px in the slot-card header but 11px uppercase in the lock-card chip** — same identifier, two treatments
3. **`<No Name>` / `<No PIN>` placeholders** look like debug output
4. **Editor still says "Conditions" (plural)** while card body says "Condition" (singular) — inconsistent UI when editing

**Code (1):**
1. **Name-edit auto-focus broken** — `selectors['name'] = '.name .name-edit-input'` doesn't match the new hero structure (no `.name` ancestor exists). PIN focus works; name focus silently fails.

### IMPORTANT (worth a follow-up)

- Lock-card slot chip + lock-name use the established a11y pattern from event-row / remove-link — just lift it
- Card-level state tinting + state chip + badge create three positive vocabularies for the same state. Consider neutral active or unify to green
- 4 different opacities for warning across one card — settle on 2-3 canonical stops
- Redundant `ENABLED` label next to a switch (the switch self-describes)
- Pencil + editable-span dual click target on name (pick one)
- Active-Unmanaged chip indistinguishable from Empty chip
- Edit inputs missing `aria-label` (placeholders aren't accessible names)
- Card titles should be real `<h2>`/`<h3>` not `<span>`
- Summary table missing `<caption>` and `scope` attributes
- "Last used: Never used" with click-through arrow opens an empty more-info — suppress arrow or reword
- Lock card "Slot N" label uppercase, slot card the same identifier title-style — pick one rendering

### NICE-TO-HAVE

- `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out on transitions
- `.collapsible-content` `max-height: 500px` clips at extreme cases
- `aria-hidden` on decorative dots
- ✓/✗ glyphs in summary badges → `mdiCheck`/`mdiClose` for visual parity
- Touch target 28px is below AAA recommendation (44px)
- Several contrast combos likely sub-AA on default themes (need browser verification)
- Helper/lock lists could use `<ul>`/`<li>` semantics
- Color contrast verification needed against HA themes

---

## Recommended path forward

Two-phase fix-up:

**Phase A (this PR — must-fix):**
1. Fix name-edit auto-focus selector (1 line)
2. Lift the existing event-row a11y pattern to the 5 broken interactions (~30 lines)
3. Add `role="alert"` / `aria-live` to error + saving (2 lines)
4. Resolve hierarchy inversion + kicker treatment + Conditions/Condition copy in the editor + placeholder copy
5. Add `e.stopPropagation()` to reveal button on managed chips

**Phase B (follow-up PR):**
- Color/opacity unification, semantic HTML upgrades, contrast verification, table semantics, motion query, NICE-TO-HAVE items

Want me to dispatch the Phase A fix-up now?

> AGENT

Phase B documented. Now the design discussion — Phase A has 4 design decisions to make:

---

### **D1. Hierarchy: name vs PIN in the hero**

Currently: `NAME label + Alice (16px)` on top, `PIN label + ••••  (22px monospace)` below. The 22px monospace dots dominate the 16px name.

The design reviewer's call: **the name should be the card's identity anchor**, not the PIN. When you open Alice's slot card, the question is "is *Alice's* PIN working?" — Alice should win.

**Three options:**

a. **Restore name to title-class above the hero** — go back to the structure you had a few iterations ago: name as the card title (~22px, semibold), pencil affordance, no `NAME` label. Hero contains only PIN + Enable. The slot kicker stays small in the header. This is closest to the original mockup intent.

b. **Keep name in hero, but make it visually dominant** — `Alice` rendered at 22px (matching PIN), pencil inline. Drop the `NAME` small-caps label since the prominent typography self-identifies. PIN stays at 22px monospace below. Both fields prominent, no labels needed.

c. **Keep current form-row, drop the label-noise** — accept that all editable fields share the form-row pattern, but drop the `NAME` and `ENABLED` labels (PIN's label can stay since `••••` doesn't self-describe). Tighter, less labeled, but the name still doesn't dominate.

My recommendation: **(a)** — restore the title position. The hero band is for *controls* (the things you change); the name is *identity* (who you're looking at). They're different categories.

### **D2. `Slot N · {entry_title}` rendering**

Slot card header: 18px title style (currently the visual title of the card).
Lock card chip: 11px uppercase kicker.

Same identifier, two treatments. The mismatch is jarring when you've been on the lock card and click into a slot.

If we go with **D1 (a)** — restore name as title — then the slot card's `Slot N · {entry_title}` naturally demotes back to 11px kicker (matching the lock card). Both cards align.

If we keep the current hero name approach (D1 b/c), the kicker stays at 18px because something has to be the visual title. Then the lock card's tiny version reads as a stylistic mismatch.

### **D3. Conditions vs Condition (editor)**

Card body says "Condition" (singular), editor toggle still says "Conditions" (plural). One-line copy fix in `slot-card-editor.ts`. Want me to also rename the YAML config key `collapsed_sections: ['conditions']` → `['condition']`? Breaking change for anyone with that in their YAML — I'd say keep the YAML key as-is and just fix the visible copy.

### **D4. Placeholder copy**

`<No Name>` and `<No PIN>` look like debug output. Recommended: italic dim "Not named" and "No PIN set" (no angle brackets). Trivial to swap. Any copy preference?

---

Walk me through your thinking on D1 first — that's the load-bearing decision the rest depend on.

> DEVELOPER

D1. option b
D2. I don't actually think this is a problem personally, let's leave it as is for now
D3. fix visible copy. For YAML, make it condition but accept conditions backwards compatibly
D4. no preference, will let you decide

> AGENT

Locked in:

- **D1 (b)**: Name at 22px in hero, drop `NAME` label, pencil inline. PIN stays 22px. Both prominent, no labels.
- **D2**: leave the kicker mismatch (slot card 18px header title, lock card 11px kicker)
- **D3**: editor copy `Conditions` → `Condition`. YAML accepts both `'condition'` and `'conditions'` for backward compat; new default uses `'condition'`.
- **D4**: my call — `Not named` and `No PIN set` (sentence case, no angle brackets, italic dim)

Dispatching Phase A fix-up combining design + a11y + the focus bug.

Done. Phase A fix-up complete.

**Summary**

- **Status:** Green across the board, committed (3b421e04), pushed.
- **Vitest:** 644 -> 669 tests (25 new).
- **Pytest:** 810 passed in ~19s.
- **Build:** Clean (only pre-existing TS2532 warnings on `_config?.show_*` ternaries that were present at baseline).
- **prek run --all-files:** all hooks Passed.
- **Commit SHA:** `3b421e04`. Push confirmed `5b10f9d6..3b421e04`.

**What changed**

- `ts/slot-card.ts` — D1 (drop NAME/ENABLED labels), D4 (placeholder copy), C1 (auto-focus selector), D3 (collapsed_sections backward compat in `setConfig`), A1/A2/A4/A5/A6/A7 (a11y on PIN, name, lock-name, collapsible header, action error, saving indicator).
- `ts/slot-card.styles.ts` — `.hero-name-value` promoted to 22px/600, `.hero-field-label` min-width dropped, `cursor:pointer` on editable name, focus-visible rings on `.hero-pin-value`, `.hero-name-value`, `.lock-name`, and `.collapsible-header` (inset for the rounded section).
- `ts/slot-card-editor.ts` — D3 editor copy "Conditions" -> "Condition", canonical write key is `'condition'`, reads accept both legacy `'conditions'` and `'condition'`.
- `ts/types.ts` — `collapsed_sections` literal union widened to `'condition' | 'conditions' | 'lock_status'` in all three interfaces (slot card config, strategy, generate-view options).
- `ts/lock-codes-card.ts` — A3 (slot-chip role/tabindex/aria-label/keydown when clickable), A8 (reveal click stopPropagation).
- `ts/lock-codes-card.styles.ts` — `:focus-visible` on `.slot-chip.clickable`.
- `ts/slot-card.integration.test.ts` / `ts/lock-codes-card.integration.test.ts` — Updated existing assertions for new copy/structure (one test rewritten to handle the new arity-1 collapsible keydown handler), added 25 new tests covering D1/D3/D4/C1 and A1–A8.

**Decisions worth flagging**

- **A2 affordance:** kept BOTH the editable name span and the pencil button as click targets (per spec recommendation), with the span keyboard-reachable via `role="button"`/`tabindex="0"`/`@keydown`. Lost-affordance risk avoided.
- **A5 collapsible header:** Added `aria-expanded` and the keydown handler. Skipped `aria-controls`/id-generation per the spec ("skip if non-trivial").
- **D3 default:** Default written when `collapsed_sections` is unset is `['condition', 'lock_status']` (canonical singular). Old YAML with `'conditions'` still collapses the section because reads check both keys.
- **D3 editor toggle:** When toggling Condition collapse, the editor strips both `'condition'` and `'conditions'` from the list before re-adding the singular, so a user touching the toggle on a card with legacy YAML migrates the key in place.
- **Test pattern for arity-1 handler sweeps:** Switched from `for…continue` (ESLint `no-continue`) to `handlers.filter(...)` + `for…of`. The collapsible Add-button stop-propagation regression test was rewritten to count total stopProp calls across the swept handlers rather than try to identify the one Add handler by arity (the new keydown handlers are also arity-1).
- **Unhandled-rejection guard in tests:** A1/A2 sweeps stub out `_handleEnabledToggle` and pass `target: { checked: false }` because the broad arity-1 handler sweep otherwise touches the `ha-switch` `@change` and produces an async rejection.

### Push + PR

- Branch pushed to `origin/phase-b/card-polish`
- PR: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1117

### Decisions where the spec left room

1. **Disabled-state header icon** — spec offered `mdiKeyOff` or `mdiLockOff`; `mdiKeyOff` is not in the installed `@mdi/js`, so I used `mdiLockOff`. Build had to fail once to surface this.
2. **Pending state accessible label** — went with option (b): `aria-hidden="true"` on the icon plus visually-hidden text inside. Applied to both `.lcm-code.pending` (lock-codes-card) and `.slot-name-pending-icon` (lock-codes-card). The slot card itself has no equivalent pending icon to label.
3. **Helpers/lock list reset CSS** — placed once in `slot-card.styles.ts` (the only card that uses these lists). The wrapping `<ul class="helpers-list">`/`<ul class="lock-list">` triggers the existing `.helpers-list > * + * { border-top }` rule correctly because `<li>` is now the direct child.
4. **Summary table row labels** — promoted `<td>` → `<th scope="row">` (proper semantics) and updated `.summary-table tbody th[scope='row']` selectors so the visual styling is preserved.
5. **`.lock-row` `:first-child/:last-child`** — original selectors broke when wrapped in `<li>`; rewrote as `.lock-list > li:first-child .lock-row` and `:last-child` equivalents.
6. **Never-used event row** — went with the spec's recommended option: drop both the chevron arrow AND the click handler, add `.event-row-static` modifier that drops cursor/hover affordances. Lays out as pure information.
7. **Condition badge icon styling** — added a small `.collapsible-badge-icon` utility (12px, `color: inherit`) so success/warning modifiers carry through to the icon color automatically.
8. **VC7 dialog microcopy test** — couldn't use a simple `.not.toContain('binary')` because the picker filter passes `binary_sensor` as a domain value. Targeted the description paragraph's static strings specifically rather than the whole dialog template.

### Things that broke and had to revisit

- **Backticks in CSS comments** in `shared-styles.ts` were parsed as JS template literal terminators inside the `css\`...\`` tag. Caught immediately, removed the backticks.
- **`mdiKeyOff` doesn't exist in `@mdi/js`** — caught at build time, swapped to `mdiLockOff` and updated the test.
- **deepStrings vs interpolated values** — `deepStrings` only joins static template segments, not interpolated scalars. Several test assertions had to switch from regex matching across attribute boundaries to either splitting into `toContain` calls or using `[\s\S]*?` for cross-line matches. The slot.slot interpolation in `aria-label="Slot ${slot.slot} PIN"` required asserting on the static `Slot ` and ` PIN"` fragments separately.
- **`yarn.lock` mutated by npm** at the start; restored to the upstream version before commit 1, no further drift.

93	fixed the WCAG-blocking interactions and the design hierarchy issues.
94	Phase B is non-blocking but worth a follow-up pass.
95	
96	**Visual / consistency:**
97	
98	- **Color opacity unification** — settle on 2-3 canonical opacity stops for
99	  state colors. Currently warning is used at 4%, 6%, 8%, 10%, 16% across
100	  the slot card alone. Decide a system (e.g., 6% backgrounds, 12% surfaces,
101	  16% chips/badges) and apply consistently.
102	- **Active state vocabulary** — slot card has three positive signals for
103	  the same Active state (card-level blue tint, green chip with dot, green
104	  badge). Decide whether Active should be neutral ("color the exception,
105	  not the norm") or unify to a single color family.
106	- **Active-Unmanaged chip on the lock card** is nearly identical to the
107	  Empty chip. Add a subtle warm-gray accent so an active unmanaged code
108	  reads as "occupied" at a glance.
109	- **`Slot N · {entry_title}` rendering inconsistency** — slot card uses
110	  18px title style, lock card uses 11px uppercase kicker style. Pick one.
111	- **Redundant `ENABLED` label** in the hero next to the switch — a switch
112	  self-describes. Consider dropping the label.
113	- **Pencil + editable-span dual click target** on the name in the hero —
114	  pick one affordance and remove the other.
115	- **`.collapsible-content { max-height: 500px }`** could clip when many
116	  helpers + a calendar entity row stack. Use `auto` with a transition shim
117	  or a much larger ceiling.
118	- **Condition summary badge color** — allowing currently uses primary blue
119	  tint instead of success green. Switch to success-color treatment so
120	  green = good, warning = needs attention everywhere.
121	- **`Helpers` sublabel** uses 10px while other small-caps labels use 11px.
122	  Unify to one scale.
123	- **Replace ✓ / ✗ glyphs** in summary badges with `mdiCheck` / `mdiClose`
124	  for visual parity with the rest of the card chrome.
125	- **Card-header icon bubble semantics** — slot card uses a generic key
126	  icon, lock card uses a lock icon. Decide whether the bubble is "this is
127	  an LCM card" (consistent) or surfaces state on the slot card (key when
128	  active, clock when blocked, lock-off when disabled).
129	- **Dialog microcopy** — "Pick a calendar, schedule, binary sensor, switch,
130	  or input boolean" enumerates technical domains. Consider "Pick a
131	  calendar, schedule, helper, or any on/off entity" for non-power users.
132	
133	**Accessibility:**
134	
135	- **Color contrast verification** against HA default light + dark themes.
136	  Likely sub-AA combinations to check:
137	  - `.hero-field-label` on the hero tinted background.
138	  - `.lcm-code.off` (`disabled-text-color`) on `--lcm-section-bg` — likely
139	    the worst case.
140	  - `.lock-synced-time` (11px secondary-text).
141	  - `.summary-cell-zero` on numeric "0" cells — these convey data, not
142	    just decoration.
143	  - `.action-error` (white on `--error-color, #db4437`) — about 4.21:1,
144	    below AA for normal text. Use a darker red or bump font weight.
145	- **`prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out** for transitions — collapsible
146	  chevron rotation, content max-height animation, slot chip hover
147	  translate, editable hover background.
148	- **`aria-hidden="true"`** on decorative dots in `.state-chip .dot` and
149	  `.lcm-badge .dot` (and the `.lcm-code-pending-icon` clock prefix).
150	- **Edit inputs missing accessible names** — name/PIN inputs and
151	  slot-code-input have placeholders but no `aria-label` (placeholders
152	  are not accessible names).
153	- **Card titles should be real headings** — `.card-header-title` and
154	  `.header-title` are `<span>`s. HA stock cards use `<h2>`/`<h3>`.
155	- **Helper / lock lists** could be `<ul>`/`<li>` so screen readers
156	  announce the item count.
157	- **Conditions/Lock Status section titles** inside collapsible headers
158	  could be `<h3>`s for heading navigation.
159	- **Summary table missing semantics** — add
160	  `<caption class="visually-hidden">` and `scope="col"` / `scope="row"`.
161	- **Suspended banner** on lock card needs `role="status"` (persistent
162	  state info, but `alert` would be too aggressive).
163	- **Touch targets** — pencil and reveal buttons at 28px pass WCAG 2.5.5
164	  AA (24px) but miss the 44px AAA recommendation. Action error dismiss
165	  button is borderline 24px.
166	- **Lock card "Last used: Never used" with clickable arrow** opens an
167	  empty more-info dialog. Either suppress the arrow or reword.
168	- **State chip color-only differentiation** — `.lcm-code.off` vs
169	  `.lcm-code.pending` distinguish via clock-icon prefix only. Add
170	  `aria-label` to the icon or visually-hidden text inside the pending
171	  span.
172	- **Collapsible badge symbols (✓/✗)** — most screen readers say "check
173	  mark"/"ballot X". Add `aria-label="Allowing access: {name}"` on the
174	  parent badge.
175	
176	## Process
177	
178	- `CLAUDE.md` points to `AGENTS.md`; update `AGENTS.md` after architecture
179	  changes.
180	- Review TODOs after completing current work, when starting new features, during
181	  refactoring sessions, or on `/todos`.
182	
```

> AGENT

All three Copilot findings on PR #1117 addressed in `3c2294a4`:

1. **Overlay status accessibility** — replaced the ✓/✗ glyph in `aria-label` with a plain "Allowing access"/"Blocking access" label, and the visible glyph swapped from text to an `aria-hidden` mdi icon (mdiCheck/mdiClose). Visual unchanged; screen readers now announce the meaning instead of "check mark"/"ballot X".

2. **Touch target WCAG citation** — corrected from SC 2.5.5 (which is AAA in WCAG 2.1) to SC 2.5.8 (the actual AA 24px minimum introduced in WCAG 2.2).

3. **Action error contrast** — switched from `var(--error-color, #db4437)` (~4.21:1, fails AA at 14px) to `var(--lcm-error-color, #b00020)` (~7.6:1, passes AA comfortably). The font-weight bump alone wasn't sufficient since WCAG 1.4.3's bold-text threshold only kicks in at ≥14px bold = 18.66px effective, not 14px.

> AGENT

The bug is `align-items: center` on `.slot-top` — when badges stack to two rows, the slot label centers against the middle of the stack (so it visually sits *between* the two badges). In the empty chip with only one badge, label and badge align perfectly. The user prefers that — fixable by aligning the label to the top of the badge stack.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- This is a classic flex-alignment pitfall: when one child has variable height (the badge stack), `align-items: center` produces visually different positions for the other child as the variable child grows. The fix is to anchor to a stable edge (start) so the label's position is independent of badge count.
- Aligning to the top also matches the conventional reading order — labels (identifiers) typically sit at the top-left, with secondary metadata (badges) flowing below or to the right. Centering inverts that hierarchy.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

  "file_path": "/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/pin_generator.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Random PIN generation with unsafe-pattern filtering.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\n\n# Common 4-digit PINs that should never be generated.\n# Source: composite of public PIN-frequency studies (Berry, DataGenetics).\nCOMMON_WEAK_PINS_4: frozenset[str] = frozenset(\n    {\n        \"0000\",\n        \"1004\",\n        \"1010\",\n        \"1111\",\n        \"1122\",\n        \"1212\",\n        \"1234\",\n        \"1313\",\n        \"2000\",\n        \"2001\",\n        \"2222\",\n        \"3333\",\n        \"4321\",\n        \"4444\",\n        \"5555\",\n        \"6666\",\n        \"6969\",\n        \"7777\",\n        \"8888\",\n        \"9999\",\n    }\n)\n\nMIN_PIN_LENGTH = 4\nMAX_PIN_LENGTH = 12\nDEFAULT_PIN_LENGTH = 4\n\n\ndef is_unsafe_pin(pin: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Return True if the PIN matches a known weak/unsafe pattern.\n\n    Rejects all-same digits, fully sequential ascending or descending\n    (with wrap at 9-to-0 / 0-to-9), repeating sub-sequence patterns\n    (1212, 123123, etc.), and for 4-digit PINs the common-PIN list\n    derived from public leak studies.\n    \"\"\"\n    n = len(pin)\n    if n == 0:\n        return True\n\n    # All same digits.\n    if len(set(pin)) == 1:\n        return True\n\n    # Repeating sub-sequence: for some k that divides n, the first k digits\n    # repeated n/k times equals the pin (k < n so we don't trivially match\n    # the whole pin against itself).\n    for k in range(1, n):\n        if n % k == 0 and pin[:k] * (n // k) == pin:\n            return True\n\n    # Fully sequential ascending or descending, with wrap at 9-to-0 / 0-to-9.\n    digits = [int(c) for c in pin]\n    asc = all((digits[i] + 1) % 10 == digits[i + 1] for i in range(n - 1))\n    desc = all((digits[i] - 1) % 10 == digits[i + 1] for i in range(n - 1))\n    if asc or desc:\n        return True\n\n    # Common 4-digit weak PINs (statistically the most-guessed values).\n    if n == 4 and pin in COMMON_WEAK_PINS_4:\n        return True\n\n    return False\n\n\ndef generate_pin(length: int = DEFAULT_PIN_LENGTH) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    Generate a cryptographically-random PIN of ``length`` digits.\n\n    Retries until the candidate passes ``is_unsafe_pin``. Uses ``secrets``\n    for entropy. A safety cap of 100 attempts protects against pathological\n    edge cases (e.g. a future filter change rejecting a much larger fraction\n    of the space).\n    \"\"\"\n    if not MIN_PIN_LENGTH <= length <= MAX_PIN_LENGTH:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"length must be between {MIN_PIN_LENGTH} and {MAX_PIN_LENGTH}\"\n        )\n    for _ in range(100):\n        candidate = \"\".join(str(secrets.randbelow(10)) for _ in range(length))\n        if not is_unsafe_pin(candidate):\n            return candidate\n    raise RuntimeError(\n        f\"Failed to generate a safe PIN of length {length} after 100 attempts\"\n    )\n"
}

def test_common_weak_pins_unsafe(self, pin: str) -> None:\n        assert is_unsafe_pin(pin)\n\n    @pytest.mark.parametrize(\"pin\", [\"5739\", \"8027\", \"4691\", \"3582\"])\n    def The errors come from `${... : nothing}` in attribute expressions. `nothing` is Lit's official "remove this attribute" sentinel, but the typedefs expect `string | undefined` here, so TS warns. The clean fix is `ifDefined` from `lit/directives/if-defined.js`:

> AGENT

The errors are TypeScript complaining about `${... : nothing}` in attribute expressions. At runtime, Lit's `nothing` sentinel does the right thing (removes the attribute), but the `*.d.ts` types for attribute bindings expect `string | undefined`, not `typeof nothing`. The build passes; it's IDE noise.

Two ways to silence cleanly:

1. **`ifDefined(undefined)`** from `lit/directives/if-defined.js` — TS-clean, semantically identical:
   ```ts
   import { ifDefined } from 'lit/directives/if-defined.js';
   title=${ifDefined(isClickable ? 'Click to manage this slot' : undefined)}
   ```

2. **Cast `nothing as unknown as string | undefined`** — works but uglier

Since this is a 4-line side fix and we're on the `feat/generate-pin-service` branch, want me to either (a) tack it onto a separate small PR after this one, or (b) include it here since it's a tiny pure typing cleanup? Or leave it as IDE noise and move on?

For now finishing the generate_pin commit so this branch stays focused. Continuing.

> AGENT

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
In Lit, standard HTML attributes (`title`, `role`, `tabindex`) get type-checked against `HTMLElement`'s string-typed properties — so `nothing` (a unique symbol) fails the type check even though it works at runtime. `ifDefined(undefined)` is the typed escape hatch: the directive returns a value compatible with the attribute's expected type, but at runtime it removes the attribute entirely. `aria-*` attributes and `@event` listeners don't have the same strict typing in Lit, which is why those `: nothing` arms work fine.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────

The same\npattern was used for the `title` on the editable code span.\n\nSwitching to `ifDefined(<value> | undefined)` keeps the runtime semantics\n(\"emit attribute if defined, omit it otherwise\") while satisfying the\nTypeScript typings. }

> AGENT

Both PRs are up:

- **PR #1118** — `generate_pin` service: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1118
- **PR #1119** — TS attribute typing fix + slot-card typing cleanups + TODO.md trim: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1119

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
A subtle bit of Lit ergonomics worth keeping in mind: `nothing` and `ifDefined(undefined)` look like alternatives, but they target different layers. `nothing` is a runtime sentinel that Lit's renderer recognizes; it's typed as a distinct symbol, so it only fits in slots whose types are loose (event handlers, `aria-*`, child positions). `ifDefined` is a directive whose return type is structurally compatible with the attribute's expected string type — that's what makes it the right tool for typed HTML attributes like `title`/`role`/`tabindex`. Same effect at runtime, very different shape to the type system.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────

WIP!

Lock Code Manager allows you to manage the slots for a single lock or a group of slots. The only requirement is that a particular slot for a particular lock can only be managed by one configuration.

Let's say you have the following locks:
lock.lock_1
lock.lock_2

You could have one config entry for `lock.lock_1` and `lock.lock_2` slots 1-4 and a second config entry for `lock.lock_1` and `lock.lock_2` slots 5-8, but if you tried to create the second config entry for slots 4-8, it would fail because slot 4 is already being managed for at least one of the locks in the first config entry.

If you are trying to figure out how to automate lock codes for a rental property (as an example), you could have a config entry that manages the permanent PINs for you and your staff and a second config entry that manages the temporary PINs you assign to guests. All of the options (whether the PIN is enabled, the PIN itself, the name assigned to the slot) can be updated using the appropriate service call. For example, to update the PIN, you could call `text.set_value` on the entity ID for the slot's PIN.

While setting this up will definitely require some work, the integration is designed to maximize flexibility and give you as much control as possible.
```

# Lock Code Manager Wiki

Welcome to the Lock Code Manager wiki!

## Getting Started

## Features

- [[Blueprints]] - Usage limiting, calendar-driven PINs, and more

- [[Unsupported-Condition-Entity-Integrations]] - Condition entities that don't work with LCM
- [[Using-"Number-of-Uses"]] - Limit how many times a PIN can be used *(deprecated)*

## Advanced

- [[Advanced-Usage]] - Managing multiple config entries and automation tips

## Development

- [[Troubleshooting-Browser-Console-Logs]] - How to capture browser console logs for frontend issues

## FAQ

{
  "file_path": "/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager.wiki/Services-and-Actions.md",
  "content": "# Services and Actions\n\nLock Code Manager registers six services (now called **actions** in modern Home Assistant). Five act on a lock or a config entry directly; one is a pure helper that returns a generated PIN.\n\n| Action | What it does |\n|---|---|\n| [`lock_code_manager.set_usercode`](#set_usercode) | Write a PIN to a single slot on a managed lock, bypassing slot configuration. |\n| [`lock_code_manager.clear_usercode`](#clear_usercode) | Clear a single slot on a managed lock, bypassing slot configuration. |\n| [`lock_code_manager.set_slot_condition`](#set_slot_condition) | Attach a condition entity (calendar, schedule, etc.) to a slot. |\n| [`lock_code_manager.clear_slot_condition`](#clear_slot_condition) | Remove the condition entity from a slot. |\n| [`lock_code_manager.hard_refresh_usercodes`](#hard_refresh_usercodes) | Re-query the lock for all stored PINs (provider-dependent). |\n| [`lock_code_manager.generate_pin`](#generate_pin) | Return a cryptographically random PIN that passes safety filtering. |\n\n> **Tip:** All actions are also exposed in the UI's *Developer Tools → Actions* tab with full schema validation and help text.\n\n---\n\n## set_usercode\n\nWrite a PIN to a specific slot on a lock that LCM is currently managing. This goes through LCM's internal write path, so it respects the same rate limits, sync bookkeeping, and provider routing as the normal slot-driven flow — but **does not change the slot's configured PIN**. The next time the sync manager reconciles the slot, the configured PIN will be re-applied.\n\nThis is primarily useful for one-off automation needs (e.g. temporarily writing a PIN that an external system generated). For persistent codes, edit the slot's PIN entity instead.\n\n| Field | Required | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `lock_entity_id` | yes | lock entity | The lock to write the PIN on. Must be managed by an LCM config entry. |\n| `code_slot` | yes | int | Target slot number on the lock. |\n| `usercode` | yes | string | The PIN to write. Cannot be empty or whitespace. |\n\n**Errors:** `ServiceValidationError` if the lock isn't managed by any LCM config entry.\n\n```yaml\naction: lock_code_manager.set_usercode\ndata:\n  lock_entity_id: lock.front_door\n  code_slot: 3\n  usercode: \"9482\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## clear_usercode\n\nClear a single slot on a managed lock through LCM's internal clear path. As with `set_usercode`, this is a low-level operation that **does not change the slot's configuration** — if the slot is enabled and has a PIN configured, the sync manager will write it back on the next reconcile.\n\n| Field | Required | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `lock_entity_id` | yes | lock entity | The lock to clear the slot on. Must be managed by an LCM config entry. |\n| `code_slot` | yes | int | Slot number on the lock to clear. |\n\n**Errors:** `ServiceValidationError` if the lock isn't managed by any LCM config entry.\n\n```yaml\naction: lock_code_manager.clear_usercode\ndata:\n  lock_entity_id: lock.front_door\n  code_slot: 3\n```\n\n---\n\n## set_slot_condition\n\nAttach a condition entity to a slot. The slot becomes active only while the condition entity is in the `on` state (for calendars, this means an event is in progress). This is the action invoked by the *Wire condition entity* dialog on the slot card.\n\n| Field | Required | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `config_entry_id` | yes | config-entry id | The LCM config entry that owns the slot. |\n| `slot` | yes | int | Slot number (1–9999). |\n| `entity_id` | yes | entity | A `binary_sensor`, `calendar`, `input_boolean`, `schedule`, or `switch` entity. |\n\n**Errors:** `ServiceValidationError` if the config entry doesn't belong to LCM, the slot doesn't exist, or the entity doesn't exist.\n\n```yaml\naction: lock_code_manager.set_slot_condition\ndata:\n  config_entry_id: REDACTED\n  slot: 4\n  entity_id: calendar.guest_stay\n```\n\n> See [[Using Condition Entities|Using-Condition-Entities]] for the full list of supported entity domains and gotchas around each one.\n\n---\n\n## clear_slot_condition\n\nRemove the condition entity from a slot. After this runs, the slot's active state is governed solely by its own enabled/disabled toggle.\n\n| Field | Required | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `config_entry_id` | yes | config-entry id | The LCM config entry that owns the slot. |\n| `slot` | yes | int | Slot number (1–9999). |\n\n**Errors:** `ServiceValidationError` if the config entry doesn't belong to LCM or the slot doesn't exist.\n\n```yaml\naction: lock_code_manager.clear_slot_condition\ndata:\n  config_entry_id: REDACTED\n  slot: 4\n```\n\n---\n\n## hard_refresh_usercodes\n\nForce LCM to re-query the lock for all stored PINs. Useful when a code was set or cleared outside of LCM (manually at the keypad, by the lock's vendor app, or by another automation) and the cached state has drifted from reality.\n\nThis is a no-op for providers that don't support read-back, and a per-slot bulk read for providers that do (Z-Wave JS, Matter, etc.). See [[Provider State Management|Provider-State-Management]] for which providers support this.\n\n| Field | Required | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `entity_id` (target) | yes | lock entity | One or more lock entities to refresh. |\n\n```yaml\naction: lock_code_manager.hard_refresh_usercodes\ntarget:\n  entity_id: lock.front_door\n```\n\n---\n\n## generate_pin\n\nReturn a cryptographically random PIN (sourced from `secrets.randbelow`) that passes a safety filter. **This action does not write to any lock** — it just returns a PIN string in the response. Pair it with `set_usercode` or with a slot's PIN text entity to actually use the value.\n\nThe safety filter rejects:\n- All-same digits (`0000`, `1111`, …)\n- Fully ascending or descending sequences with wrap-around at 9↔0 (`1234`, `7890`, `9876`, `1098`, …)\n- Repeating sub-sequences that tile the PIN (`1212`, `123123`, …)\n- A curated list of common weak 4-digit PINs (`1004`, `2580`, `6969`, …)\n\n| Field | Required | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `length` | no | int (4–12) | Number of digits to generate. Defaults to `4`. |\n\n**Returns** (via `response_variable`):\n\n```yaml\npin: \"8472\"\n```\n\n**Example — generate and write to a slot's PIN text entity:**\n\n```yaml\naction: lock_code_manager.generate_pin\ndata:\n  length: 6\nresponse_variable: result\n- action: text.set_value\n  target:\n    entity_id: text.house_locks_pin_4\n  data:\n    value: \"{{ result.pin }}\"\n```\n\n**Example — rotate the PIN whenever a guest calendar event ends:**\n\n```yaml\ntrigger:\n  - platform: state\n    entity_id: calendar.guest_stay\n    to: \"off\"\naction:\n  - action: lock_code_manager.generate_pin\n    response_variable: new_pin\n  - action: text.set_value\n    target:\n      entity_id: text.guest_house_pin_3\n    data:\n      value: \"{{ new_pin.pin }}\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## Service vs. provider methods\n\nIf you're reading source code or contributing a new provider, note that the **services** documented here are user-facing actions registered on the `lock_code_manager` domain. They are distinct from the **provider methods** of the same names (`async_set_usercode`, `async_clear_usercode`) that subclasses of `BaseLock` implement to talk to specific lock integrations. See [[Adding a Provider|Adding-a-Provider]] and [[Provider State Management|Provider-State-Management]] for the provider-side API.\n"
}
```

> AGENT

I'd go with **two pages, plus a thin hub** — closer to your first instinct than one-per-card. Concretely:

**`Add-a-UI-for-lock-code-management.md`** (kept, but slimmed to ~30–40 lines): a landing/decision page covering dashboard creation basics + a "which approach should I use?" decision guide that routes to the two pages below. Keeping the URL alive matters because it's linked from the integration's docs and almost certainly bookmarked externally.

**`UI-Strategies.md`** (new): view strategy, slot section strategy, lock section strategy, legacy mode. These all share the same mental model — *let LCM generate UI for you from your config* — so they belong together. They also share schema patterns, which would be duplicated if split further.

**`Custom-Cards.md`** (new): slot card + lock codes card + code display modes. Same audience — *I'm building my own dashboard and want LCM-aware cards as building blocks*. Display modes naturally live here since they're a card-config concern, not a strategy one.

**Why not one-page-per-strategy/card:** the slot section strategy and slot card share concepts, the two section strategies share a config skeleton, and the two cards share theming + display-mode behavior. Splitting six ways means duplicating those overlaps in three pairs. You'd also end up with several quite-short pages and a sidebar that's heavier than the content justifies.

**One real trade-off to flag:** if/when the cards or strategies grow significantly (e.g. the slot card gains a deep visual-editor doc, or section strategies pick up new modes), one of the two pages can split further later. Going from 2 → 4 is easy; going from 6 → 2 is painful. That argues for starting at the coarser grain.

```
1	# Add a UI for lock code management
2	
3	Lock Code Manager provides custom Lovelace strategies and cards for managing PINs directly from your Home Assistant dashboard.
4	
5	## Dashboard
6	
7	The easiest way to get started is to create a dedicated dashboard using the Lock Code Manager
8	strategy. This automatically generates views for each of your LCM config entries.
9	
10	### Creating the Dashboard
11	
12	1. Go to **Settings > Dashboards > Add Dashboard**
13	2. Choose a name (e.g., "Lock Codes") and icon
14	3. Open the dashboard and click the pencil icon to edit
15	4. Click the three dots menu and select **Raw configuration editor**
16	5. Replace the content with:
17	
18	```yaml
19	strategy:
20	  type: custom:lock-code-manager
21	```
22	
23	### Dashboard Options
24	
25	| Option                              | Required | Default              | Description                                                 |
26	| ----------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
27	| `use_slot_cards`                    | No       | `true`               | Use streamlined slot cards instead of legacy entities cards |
28	| `show_code_sensors`                 | No       | `true`               | Show code sensors in lock status section                    |
29	| `show_conditions`                   | No       | `true`               | Show conditions section in slot cards                       |
30	| `show_lock_status`                  | No       | `true`               | Show lock status section in slot cards                      |
31	| `show_lock_sync`                    | No       | `true`               | Show sync status per lock in lock status                    |
32	| `collapsed_sections`                | No       | `[]`                 | Which sections start collapsed (empty = all expanded)       |
33	| `show_per_configuration_lock_cards` | No       | `true`               | Show lock cards in per-config-entry views                   |
34	| `show_all_lock_cards_view`          | No       | `true`               | Add a "User Codes" view with cards showing all lock codes   |
35	| `code_display`                      | No       | `masked_with_reveal` | Code visibility mode for slot cards and lock codes cards    |
36	
37	**Legacy options** (still supported but deprecated):
38	
39	- `include_code_slot_sensors` → use `show_code_sensors`
40	- `include_in_sync_sensors` → use `show_lock_sync`
41	- `code_data_view_code_display` → use `code_display`
42	- `show_all_codes_for_locks` → use `show_all_lock_cards_view` and/or `show_per_configuration_lock_cards`
43	
44	### Example Dashboard Configuration
45	
46	```yaml
47	strategy:
48	  type: custom:lock-code-manager
49	  show_all_lock_cards_view: true
50	  show_per_configuration_lock_cards: true
51	  code_display: masked_with_reveal
52	  show_lock_sync: true
53	```
54	
55	## View Strategy
56	
57	If you want to add Lock Code Manager to an existing dashboard, you can use the view strategy for a single config entry.
58	
59	### View Options
60	
61	| Option                     | Required | Default              | Description                                                  |
62	| -------------------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
63	| `config_entry_id`          | Yes*     | -                    | Config entry ID to render (use this OR config_entry_title)   |
64	| `config_entry_title`       | Yes*     | -                    | Config entry title to render (use this OR config_entry_id)   |
65	| `use_slot_cards`           | No       | `true`               | Use streamlined slot cards instead of legacy entities cards  |
66	| `show_code_sensors`        | No       | `true`               | Show code sensors in lock status section                     |
67	| `show_conditions`          | No       | `true`               | Show conditions section in slot cards                        |
68	| `show_lock_status`         | No       | `true`               | Show lock status section in slot cards                       |
69	| `show_lock_sync`           | No       | `true`               | Show sync status per lock in lock status                     |
70	| `collapsed_sections`       | No       | `[]`                 | Which sections start collapsed (empty = all expanded)        |
71	| `show_lock_cards`          | No       | `true`               | Append lock codes cards below the slot cards                 |
72	| `code_display`             | No       | `masked_with_reveal` | Code visibility mode for slot cards and lock codes cards     |
73	
74	*Either `config_entry_id` or `config_entry_title` is required, but not both.
75	
76	**Legacy options** (still supported but deprecated):
77	
78	- `include_code_slot_sensors` → use `show_code_sensors`
79	- `include_in_sync_sensors` → use `show_lock_sync`
80	- `code_data_view_code_display` → use `code_display`
81	- `show_all_codes_for_locks` → use `show_lock_cards`
82	
83	### Example View Configuration
84	
85	```yaml
86	views:
87	  - strategy:
88	      type: custom:lock-code-manager
89	      config_entry_title: House Locks
90	    icon: mdi:lock-smart
91	    title: Lock Codes
92	```
93	
94	## Section Strategies
95	
96	For advanced users building custom `sections`-type views, Lock Code Manager provides
97	section strategies that generate cards when Home Assistant renders the section.
98	
99	> **Note:** Section strategies simply render a single card (`lcm-slot` or `lcm-lock-codes`)
100	> within a grid section. You can use the cards directly in your dashboard without using
101	> section strategies - see [Custom Cards](#custom-cards) below.
102	
103	### Slot Section Strategy (`custom:lock-code-manager-slot`)
104	
105	Renders a single slot section with either the new `lcm-slot` card or legacy entities card.
106	
107	| Option              | Required | Default              | Description                                                   |
108	| ------------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
109	| `config_entry_id`   | Yes      | -                    | Config entry ID for the LCM instance                          |
110	| `slot`              | Yes      | -                    | Slot number to display                                        |
111	| `use_slot_cards`    | No       | `true`               | Use new lcm-slot card (`true`) or legacy entities card        |
112	| `code_display`      | No       | `masked_with_reveal` | Code visibility mode                                          |
113	| `show_conditions`   | No       | `true`               | Show conditions section                                       |
114	| `show_lock_status`  | No       | `true`               | Show lock status section                                      |
115	| `show_code_sensors` | No       | `true`               | Show code sensors in lock status                              |
116	| `show_lock_sync`    | No       | `true`               | Show sync status per lock                                     |
117	| `collapsed_sections`| No       | `[]`                 | Sections to collapse by default: `conditions`, `lock_status`  |
118	
119	**Example:**
120	
121	```yaml
122	views:
123	  - type: sections
124	    title: Lock Codes
125	    sections:
126	      - strategy:
127	          type: custom:lock-code-manager-slot
128	          config_entry_id: 1234567890abcdef
129	          slot: 1
130	          code_display: masked_with_reveal
131	      - strategy:
132	          type: custom:lock-code-manager-slot
133	          config_entry_id: 1234567890abcdef
134	          slot: 2
135	```
136	
137	### Lock Section Strategy (`custom:lock-code-manager-lock`)
138	
139	Renders a lock codes section showing all slots for a specific lock.
140	
141	| Option           | Required | Default              | Description                           |
142	| ---------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
143	| `lock_entity_id` | Yes      | -                    | The entity ID of the lock             |
144	| `code_display`   | No       | `masked_with_reveal` | Code visibility mode                  |
145	
146	**Example:**
147	
148	```yaml
149	views:
150	  - type: sections
151	    title: All Lock Codes
152	    sections:
153	      - strategy:
154	          type: custom:lock-code-manager-lock
155	          lock_entity_id: lock.front_door
156	          code_display: masked
157	      - strategy:
158	          type: custom:lock-code-manager-lock
159	          lock_entity_id: lock.back_door
160	```
161	
162	## Custom Cards
163	
164	Lock Code Manager provides two custom cards that can be used independently or are automatically included by the strategies.
165	
166	### Slot Card (`custom:lcm-slot`)
167	
168	The slot card displays a single code slot with inline editing, real-time WebSocket updates,
169	and collapsible sections. This is the default card used by the strategies.
170	
171	**Features:**
172	
173	- Inline editing for name, PIN, and enabled toggle
174	- Real-time updates via WebSocket
175	- Collapsible conditions and lock status sections
176	- Status badges showing active/inactive/disabled state
177	- Per-lock sync status
178	
179	**Configuration:**
180	
181	| Option               | Required | Default              | Description                                                  |
182	| -------------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
183	| `config_entry_id`    | Yes*     | -                    | Config entry ID for the LCM instance                         |
184	| `config_entry_title` | Yes*     | -                    | Config entry title (alternative to ID)                       |
185	| `slot`               | Yes      | -                    | Slot number to display                                       |
186	| `code_display`       | No       | `masked_with_reveal` | How to display codes (see below)                             |
187	| `show_conditions`    | No       | `true`               | Show the conditions section                                  |
188	| `show_lock_status`   | No       | `true`               | Show the lock status section                                 |
189	| `show_code_sensors`  | No       | `true`               | Show code sensors in lock status                             |
190	| `show_lock_sync`     | No       | `true`               | Show sync status per lock                                    |
191	| `collapsed_sections` | No       | `[]`                 | Which sections start collapsed (empty = all expanded)        |
192	
193	*Either `config_entry_id` or `config_entry_title` is required, but not both.
194	
195	**Example:**
196	
197	```yaml
198	type: custom:lcm-slot
199	config_entry_id: 1234567890abcdef
200	slot: 1
201	code_display: masked_with_reveal
202	collapsed_sections:
203	  - lock_status
204	```
205	
206	### Lock Codes Card (`custom:lcm-lock-codes`)
207	
208	The lock codes card displays all code slots for a specific lock. It shows status badges,
209	supports inline editing for unmanaged slots, and provides click-to-navigate for LCM-managed
210	slots.
211	
212	**Features:**
213	
214	- Shows all slots on a lock with their current codes
215	- Status badges (Active, Inactive, Disabled, Empty)
216	- Sync status indicators
217	- Inline editing for slots not managed by LCM
218	- Click managed slots to navigate to their config entry
219	- Reveal button for masked codes
220	
221	**Configuration:**
222	
223	| Option           | Required | Default              | Description                                    |
224	| ---------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
225	| `lock_entity_id` | Yes      | -                    | The entity ID of the lock to display codes for |
226	| `title`          | No       | Lock name            | Custom title for the card                      |
227	| `code_display`   | No       | `masked_with_reveal` | How to display codes (see below)               |
228	
229	**Example:**
230	
231	```yaml
232	type: custom:lcm-lock-codes
233	lock_entity_id: lock.front_door
234	title: Front Door Codes
235	code_display: masked_with_reveal
236	```
237	
238	## Code Display Modes
239	
240	Both cards support three code display modes:
241	
242	| Mode                 | Description                                              |
243	| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
244	| `masked`             | Codes are always hidden (shown as bullets)               |
245	| `unmasked`           | Codes are always visible                                 |
246	| `masked_with_reveal` | Codes are masked but can be revealed with a toggle button (default) |
247	
248	## Legacy Mode
249	
250	If you prefer the old entities-card based UI, set `use_slot_cards: false` in your strategy configuration:
251	
252	```yaml
253	strategy:
254	  type: custom:lock-code-manager
255	  use_slot_cards: false
256	  include_code_slot_sensors: true
257	```
258	
259	**Note:** When using legacy mode (`use_slot_cards: false`), installing the
260	[fold-entity-row](https://github.com/thomasloven/lovelace-fold-entity-row) card provides
261	a cleaner UI by collapsing related entities into expandable rows.
262	
263	### Example
264	![dashboard](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/assets/7746625/c5d02014-923f-44e8-876a-35642d34c381)
265	
```

8	import { HomeAssistant } from './ha_type_stubs';
9	import { slugify } from './slugify';
10	import { createErrorView } from './strategy-utils';
11	import {
12	    GetConfigEntriesResponse,
13	    LockCodeManagerConfigEntryDataResponse,
14	    LockCodeManagerDashboardStrategyConfig,
15	    LockInfo
16	} from './types';
17	
18	/** Message shown when no LCM configurations exist */
19	export const NO_CONFIG_MESSAGE = '# No Lock Code Manager configurations found!';
20	
21	/** Zero-width space used as placeholder title for single-view hack */
22	export const ZERO_WIDTH_SPACE = '​';
23	
24	export class LockCodeManagerDashboardStrategy extends ReactiveElement {
25	    static async generate(config: LockCodeManagerDashboardStrategyConfig, hass: HomeAssistant) {
26	        const configEntries = await hass.callWS<GetConfigEntriesResponse>({
27	            domain: 'lock_code_manager',
28	            type: 'config_entries/get'
29	        });
30	
31	        if (configEntries.length === 0) {
32	            return {
33	                title: 'Lock Code Manager',
34	                views: [createErrorView(NO_CONFIG_MESSAGE)]
35	            };
36	        }
37	
38	        // show_per_configuration_lock_cards controls whether lock cards appear in per-config views
39	        // It feeds show_lock_cards to each view strategy
40	        // Support legacy show_all_codes_for_locks option for backwards compatibility
41	        const showLockCardsInViews =
42	            config.show_per_configuration_lock_cards ??
43	            config.show_all_codes_for_locks ??
44	            DEFAULT_SHOW_PER_CONFIGURATION_LOCK_CARDS;
45	
46	        const views: object[] = configEntries.map((configEntry) => {
47	            return {
48	                path: slugify(configEntry.title),
49	                strategy: {
50	                    code_display: config.code_display,
51	                    collapsed_sections: config.collapsed_sections,
52	                    condition_helpers: config.condition_helpers?.[configEntry.entry_id],
53	                    config_entry_id: configEntry.entry_id,
54	                    show_code_sensors: config.show_code_sensors,
55	                    show_conditions: config.show_conditions,
56	                    show_lock_cards: showLockCardsInViews,
57	                    show_lock_status: config.show_lock_status,
58	                    show_lock_sync: config.show_lock_sync,
59	                    type: 'custom:lock-code-manager',
60	                    use_slot_cards: config.use_slot_cards
61	                },
62	                title: configEntry.title
63	            };
64	        });
65	
66	        // show_all_lock_cards_view controls whether the "User Codes" view is added
67	        // Support legacy show_all_codes_for_locks option for backwards compatibility
68	        const showAllLockCardsView =
69	            config.show_all_lock_cards_view ??
70	            config.show_all_codes_for_locks ??
71	            DEFAULT_SHOW_ALL_LOCK_CARDS_VIEW;
72	        if (showAllLockCardsView) {
73	            const locksMap = new Map<string, LockInfo>();
74	            await Promise.all(
75	                configEntries.map(async (configEntry) => {
76	                    const data = await hass.callWS<LockCodeManagerConfigEntryDataResponse>({
77	                        config_entry_id: configEntry.entry_id,
78	                        type: 'lock_code_manager/get_config_entry_data'
79	                    });
80	                    data.locks.forEach((lock) => locksMap.set(lock.entity_id, lock));
81	                })
82	            );
83	
84	            const sortedLocks = Array.from(locksMap.values()).sort((a, b) =>
85	                a.name.localeCompare(b.name, undefined, { sensitivity: 'base' })
86	            );
87	
88	            // Create sections for each lock (same layout as view strategy)
89	            const sections =
90	                sortedLocks.length > 0
91	                    ? sortedLocks.map((lock) => {
92	                          return {
93	                              cards: [
94	                                  {
95	                                      code_display: config.code_display ?? DEFAULT_CODE_DISPLAY,
96	                                      lock_entity_id: lock.entity_id,
97	                                      type: 'custom:lcm-lock-codes'
98	                                  }
99	                              ],
100	                              title: lock.name,
101	                              type: 'grid'
102	                          };
103	                      })
104	                    : undefined;
105	
106	            const cards =
107	                sortedLocks.length === 0
108	                    ? [
109	                          {
110	                              content: '# No locks found to display.',
111	                              type: 'markdown'
112	                          }
113	                      ]
114	                    : undefined;
115	
116	            views.push({
117	                ...(cards && { cards }),
118	                icon: 'mdi:lock-smart',
119	                path: 'user-codes',
120	                ...(sections && { sections }),
121	                title: 'User Codes',
122	                ...(sections && { type: 'sections' })
123	            });
124	        }
125	
126	        // Single view hack: add placeholder to force tab visibility
127	        if (views.length === 1) {
128	            views.push({ title: ZERO_WIDTH_SPACE });
129	        }
130	
131	        return {
132	            title: 'Lock Code Manager',
133	            views
134	        };
135	    }
136	}
137	
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager.wiki/Add-a-UI-for-lock-code-management.md",
  "content": "# Add a UI for lock code management\n\nLock Code Manager ships custom dashboard **strategies** (which generate Lovelace UI for you) and custom **cards** (which you compose yourself into a dashboard). Most people pick one or the other based on how much control they want.\n\n## Which approach should I pick?\n\n| You want… | Use… | Documented in |\n|---|---|---|\n| The fastest possible setup — open a dashboard, paste 2 lines, done | Dashboard strategy | [[UI Strategies → Dashboard strategy\\|UI-Strategies#dashboard-strategy]] |\n| To add a Lock Code Manager view to a dashboard you already use | View strategy | [[UI Strategies → View strategy\\|UI-Strategies#view-strategy]] |\n| To drop one slot or one lock into a `sections`-type view alongside non-LCM cards | Section strategies | [[UI Strategies → Section strategies\\|UI-Strategies#section-strategies]] |\n| To fully hand-author a dashboard, picking exactly which cards live where | Custom cards | [[Custom Cards\\|Custom-Cards]] |\n| The pre-2.0 entities-card UI | Legacy mode | [[UI Strategies → Legacy mode\\|UI-Strategies#legacy-mode]] |\n\n> Strategies and custom cards aren't mutually exclusive — a strategy ultimately just emits the same custom cards documented under [[Custom Cards|Custom-Cards]]. You can mix-and-match.\n\n## Quick start: dashboard strategy\n\nThis generates a dashboard with one view per LCM config entry, plus a \"User Codes\" view that shows every code on every managed lock.\n\n1. Go to **Settings → Dashboards → Add Dashboard**.\n2. Choose a name (e.g. *Lock Codes*) and an icon.\n3. Open the dashboard and click the pencil icon to edit.\n4. Click the three-dot menu → **Raw configuration editor**.\n5. Replace the contents with:\n\n   ```yaml\n   strategy:\n     type: custom:lock-code-manager\n   ```\n\nThat's it — every config entry is auto-discovered. To customize what appears (collapsed sections, code-display mode, which sub-views to render, condition helper entities, etc.), see [[UI Strategies → Dashboard strategy options|UI-Strategies#dashboard-strategy-options]].\n\n## Example\n\n![dashboard](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/assets/7746625/c5d02014-923f-44e8-876a-35642d34c381)\n"
}
