{
  "file_path": "/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager.wiki/UI-Strategies.md",
  "content": "# UI Strategies\n\nStrategies are Lovelace generators: you write a small block of YAML, and Home Assistant calls into Lock Code Manager at render time to produce the views, sections, and cards. The strategy reads your LCM config entries directly, so it stays in sync as slots and locks are added or removed without you having to edit the dashboard.\n\nLCM ships **four** strategies, all under the `custom:lock-code-manager*` family:\n\n- [Dashboard strategy](#dashboard-strategy) — generates an entire dashboard.\n- [View strategy](#view-strategy) — generates a single view inside a dashboard.\n- [Slot section strategy](#slot-section-strategy) — generates a single slot card inside a `sections`-type view.\n- [Lock section strategy](#lock-section-strategy) — generates a single lock-codes card inside a `sections`-type view.\n\nFor the user-facing decision guide on which one to pick, see [[Add a UI for lock code management|Add-a-UI-for-lock-code-management]].\n\n---\n\n## Dashboard strategy\n\n**Type:** `custom:lock-code-manager`\n\nGenerates a complete dashboard:\n\n- One view per LCM config entry (slot cards stacked, optionally followed by lock-codes cards).\n- An optional **User Codes** view containing one lock-codes card per managed lock.\n\n```yaml\nstrategy:\n  type: custom:lock-code-manager\n```\n\n### Dashboard strategy options\n\n| Option | Type | Default | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `code_display` | `masked` \\| `unmasked` \\| `masked_with_reveal` | `masked_with_reveal` | Code-display mode applied to every slot card and lock-codes card. See [[Custom Cards#code-display-modes\\|Custom-Cards#code-display-modes]]. |\n| `use_slot_cards` | bool | `true` | Use the modern slot card. Set `false` for the pre-2.0 entities-card layout (see [Legacy mode](#legacy-mode)). |\n| `show_conditions` | bool | `true` | Show the *Conditions* section in slot cards. |\n| `show_lock_status` | bool | `true` | Show the *Lock status* section in slot cards. |\n| `show_code_sensors` | bool | `true` | Within *Lock status*, show the actual on-lock code sensor. |\n| `show_lock_sync` | bool | `true` | Within *Lock status*, show per-lock sync state (in-sync, out-of-sync, syncing, suspended). |\n| `collapsed_sections` | array of `condition` \\| `conditions` \\| `lock_status` | `[]` | Sections that start collapsed in slot cards. (Both `condition` and `conditions` are accepted for the conditions section.) |\n| `show_per_configuration_lock_cards` | bool | `true` | Append lock-codes cards to each per-config-entry view. |\n| `show_all_lock_cards_view` | bool | `true` | Add the *User Codes* view that shows every lock's full code list. |\n| `condition_helpers` | `Record<config_entry_id, Record<slot_num, entity_id[]>>` | none | Extra helper entity IDs (toggles, schedules, etc.) shown alongside the configured condition entity inside the slot card. Lets users flip helpers from the dashboard without editing the slot. |\n\n### Deprecated dashboard options\n\nThese still work as backward-compatibility aliases but should be replaced:\n\n| Deprecated | Use instead |\n|---|---|\n| `include_code_slot_sensors` | `show_code_sensors` |\n| `include_in_sync_sensors` | `show_lock_sync` |\n| `code_data_view_code_display` | `code_display` |\n| `show_all_codes_for_locks` | `show_all_lock_cards_view` and/or `show_per_configuration_lock_cards` |\n\n### Example\n\n```yaml\nstrategy:\n  type: custom:lock-code-manager\n  code_display: masked_with_reveal\n  show_all_lock_cards_view: true\n  show_per_configuration_lock_cards: false\n  collapsed_sections:\n    - lock_status\n  condition_helpers:\n    REDACTED:\n      4: [input_boolean.guest_arrived, schedule.guest_quiet_hours]\n```\n\n---\n\n## View strategy\n\n**Type:** `custom:lock-code-manager` (in a `views[].strategy` slot)\n\nGenerates a single view for **one** config entry. Use this to add LCM into a dashboard you already maintain.\n\n```yaml\nviews:\n  - strategy:\n      type: custom:lock-code-manager\n      config_entry_title: House Locks\n    icon: mdi:lock-smart\n    title: Lock Codes\n```\n\n### View strategy options\n\nEither `config_entry_id` *or* `config_entry_title` is required — not both.\n\n| Option | Type | Default | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `config_entry_id` | string | — | LCM config entry ID. Use this for stability across renames. |\n| `config_entry_title` | string | — | LCM config entry title. Convenient for hand-edited YAML. |\n| `code_display` | `masked` \\| `unmasked` \\| `masked_with_reveal` | `masked_with_reveal` | Code-display mode for every card the view emits. |\n| `use_slot_cards` | bool | `true` | Use the modern slot card vs. legacy entities cards. |\n| `show_conditions` | bool | `true` | Show the *Conditions* section in slot cards. |\n| `show_lock_status` | bool | `true` | Show the *Lock status* section in slot cards. |\n| `show_code_sensors` | bool | `true` | Show the on-lock code sensor inside *Lock status*. |\n| `show_lock_sync` | bool | `true` | Show per-lock sync state inside *Lock status*. |\n| `collapsed_sections` | array of `condition` \\| `conditions` \\| `lock_status` | `[]` | Sections that start collapsed. |\n| `show_lock_cards` | bool | `true` | Append lock-codes cards below the slot cards. |\n| `condition_helpers` | `Record<slot_num, entity_id[]>` | none | Extra helper entity IDs to surface in each slot card, keyed by slot number. |\n\n### Deprecated view options\n\n| Deprecated | Use instead |\n|---|---|\n| `include_code_slot_sensors` | `show_code_sensors` |\n| `include_in_sync_sensors` | `show_lock_sync` |\n| `code_data_view_code_display` | `code_display` |\n| `show_all_codes_for_locks` | `show_lock_cards` |\n\n---\n\n## Section strategies\n\nFor dashboards using `type: sections` views, LCM provides two strategies that each emit a **single card** inside a grid section. They're a thin wrapper over the corresponding [custom card](Custom-Cards) — useful when you want strategy-style auto-resolution of types but in a hand-built sections layout. If you'd rather just place the cards directly, use them from [[Custom Cards|Custom-Cards]].\n\n### Slot section strategy\n\n**Type:** `custom:lock-code-manager-slot`\n\nRenders a single slot card.\n\n| Option | Type | Default | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `config_entry_id` | string | — *(required)* | LCM config entry that owns the slot. |\n| `slot` | int | — *(required)* | Slot number to render. |\n| `code_display` | `masked` \\| `unmasked` \\| `masked_with_reveal` | `masked_with_reveal` | Code-display mode. |\n| `use_slot_cards` | bool | `true` | Use the modern slot card vs. legacy entities card. |\n| `show_conditions` | bool | `true` | Show the *Conditions* section. |\n| `show_lock_status` | bool | `true` | Show the *Lock status* section. |\n| `show_code_sensors` | bool | `true` | Show the on-lock code sensor inside *Lock status*. |\n| `show_lock_sync` | bool | `true` | Show per-lock sync state inside *Lock status*. |\n| `show_lock_count` | bool | `true` | Show the lock-count badge in the card header. |\n| `collapsed_sections` | array of `condition` \\| `conditions` \\| `lock_status` | `[]` | Sections that start collapsed. |\n| `condition_helpers` | array of entity IDs | none | Extra helper entities surfaced inside the slot card. |\n\n```yaml\nviews:\n  - type: sections\n    title: Lock Codes\n    sections:\n      - strategy:\n          type: custom:lock-code-manager-slot\n          config_entry_id: REDACTED\n          slot: 1\n      - strategy:\n          type: custom:lock-code-manager-slot\n          config_entry_id: REDACTED\n          slot: 2\n          collapsed_sections: [lock_status]\n```\n\n### Lock section strategy\n\n**Type:** `custom:lock-code-manager-lock`\n\nRenders a single lock-codes card.\n\n| Option | Type | Default | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `lock_entity_id` | lock entity | — *(required)* | The lock to display codes for. |\n| `code_display` | `masked` \\| `unmasked` \\| `masked_with_reveal` | `masked_with_reveal` | Code-display mode. |\n\n```yaml\nviews:\n  - type: sections\n    title: All Lock Codes\n    sections:\n      - strategy:\n          type: custom:lock-code-manager-lock\n          lock_entity_id: lock.front_door\n          code_display: masked\n      - strategy:\n          type: custom:lock-code-manager-lock\n          lock_entity_id: lock.back_door\n```\n\n---\n\n## Legacy mode\n\nSetting `use_slot_cards: false` on the dashboard, view, or slot-section strategy falls back to the pre-2.0 layout, which uses Home Assistant's stock entities cards instead of the modern slot card. This exists for users who hand-customized the old layout and aren't ready to migrate.\n\n```yaml\nstrategy:\n  type: custom:lock-code-manager\n  use_slot_cards: false\n  show_code_sensors: true\n```\n\n> **Recommended add-on:** install the [fold-entity-row](https://github.com/thomasloven/lovelace-fold-entity-row) custom card. The legacy layout looks much cleaner with collapsible related-entity rows.\n\nLegacy mode receives bug fixes but no new features — `condition_helpers`, `show_lock_count`, and the modern sync-status display are slot-card-only.\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager.wiki/Custom-Cards.md",
  "content": "# Custom Cards\n\nLock Code Manager registers two custom Lovelace cards. They're the building blocks the [[UI Strategies|UI-Strategies]] generate, but you can also place them yourself anywhere in a hand-built dashboard.\n\n- [Slot card](#slot-card-customlcm-slot) — one slot, with inline editing.\n- [Lock codes card](#lock-codes-card-customlcm-lock-codes) — every slot on one lock, with status badges.\n\nBoth cards have **visual editors** in the dashboard UI, so you can configure them by clicking *Edit dashboard → Add card → Custom: Lock Code Manager Slot Card / Lock Codes Card* without writing YAML. The tables below document every option for users editing in YAML or building strategies.\n\n---\n\n## Slot card (`custom:lcm-slot`)\n\nDisplays a single LCM-managed code slot with inline editing of name/PIN/enabled state, real-time updates over WebSocket, and collapsible *Conditions* and *Lock status* sections.\n\n### Features\n\n- Inline editing of the slot name, PIN, and enabled toggle (no need to dive into the integration's options page).\n- Real-time updates: name, PIN, and condition entity changes pushed live over a WebSocket subscription.\n- Status badges at the card header: active, inactive, disabled, pending sync, suspended.\n- *Conditions* section showing the configured condition entity (calendar, schedule, binary_sensor, etc.) with a *Wire condition entity* dialog for adding one inline.\n- Optional **condition helper** entities (toggles, schedules, etc.) surfaced under the condition entity for quick access from the dashboard.\n- *Lock status* section showing per-lock sync state and (optionally) the actual code currently on each lock.\n- Lock-count badge in the header showing how many locks the slot is configured on.\n\n### Configuration\n\nEither `config_entry_id` *or* `config_entry_title` is required — not both.\n\n| Option | Type | Default | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `config_entry_id` | string | — | LCM config entry ID. Use this for stability across renames. |\n| `config_entry_title` | string | — | LCM config entry title. Convenient for hand-edited YAML. |\n| `slot` | int | — *(required)* | Slot number to display. |\n| `code_display` | `masked` \\| `unmasked` \\| `masked_with_reveal` | `masked_with_reveal` | How code values render in the *Lock status* section. See [Code display modes](#code-display-modes). |\n| `show_conditions` | bool | `true` | Show the *Conditions* section. |\n| `show_lock_status` | bool | `true` | Show the *Lock status* section. |\n| `show_code_sensors` | bool | `true` | Show the on-lock code sensor inside *Lock status*. |\n| `show_lock_sync` | bool | `true` | Show per-lock sync state inside *Lock status*. |\n| `show_lock_count` | bool | `true` | Show the lock-count badge in the card header. |\n| `collapsed_sections` | array of `condition` \\| `conditions` \\| `lock_status` | `[]` | Sections that start collapsed. (Both `condition` and `conditions` are accepted.) |\n| `condition_helpers` | array of entity IDs | none | Extra helper entities (input_booleans, schedules, switches, etc.) surfaced underneath the condition entity for quick toggling from the dashboard. |\n\n### Example\n\n```yaml\ntype: custom:lcm-slot\nconfig_entry_id: REDACTED\nslot: 1\ncode_display: masked_with_reveal\ncollapsed_sections:\n  - lock_status\ncondition_helpers:\n  - input_boolean.guest_arrived\n  - schedule.guest_quiet_hours\n```\n\n---\n\n## Lock codes card (`custom:lcm-lock-codes`)\n\nDisplays all code slots for a specific lock — both LCM-managed and unmanaged — with status badges and inline editing for the unmanaged ones.\n\n### Features\n\n- Shows every slot on the lock with its current code (subject to [Code display modes](#code-display-modes)).\n- Status chips per slot: *Active*, *Inactive*, *Disabled*, *Empty*, *Pending sync*.\n- Sync-status indicators with distinct visual treatment for in-sync, out-of-sync, syncing, and suspended states.\n- LCM-managed slots are clickable: clicking navigates to the slot's config entry view.\n- Unmanaged slots are inline-editable: click the code value to set or clear it (uses `set_usercode` / `clear_usercode` from [[Services and Actions|Services-and-Actions]]).\n- Reveal/hide button for masked codes when `code_display: masked_with_reveal`.\n\n### Configuration\n\n| Option | Type | Default | Description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `lock_entity_id` | lock entity | — *(required)* | The lock to display codes for. |\n| `title` | string | lock's friendly name | Custom title for the card. |\n| `code_display` | `masked` \\| `unmasked` \\| `masked_with_reveal` | `masked_with_reveal` | How code values render. See [Code display modes](#code-display-modes). |\n\n### Example\n\n```yaml\ntype: custom:lcm-lock-codes\nlock_entity_id: lock.front_door\ntitle: Front Door Codes\ncode_display: masked_with_reveal\n```\n\n---\n\n## Code display modes\n\nBoth cards (and every strategy that wraps them) accept the same `code_display` values:\n\n| Mode | Description |\n|---|---|\n| `masked` | Codes are always hidden as bullets. Length is preserved when known. |\n| `unmasked` | Codes are always visible in plain text. |\n| `masked_with_reveal` | *(default)* Codes are masked but can be revealed individually with a per-card toggle button. |\n\n> **Privacy reminder:** `masked` only hides codes in this card's UI — it doesn't redact PIN values from logs, the underlying `text.*` PIN entities, the device activity log, or the recorder database. See [[PIN Codes Visible in Activity Log|PIN-Codes-Visible-in-Activity-Log]] for the broader picture.\n"
}

1	# UI Strategies
2	
3	Strategies are Lovelace generators: you write a small block of YAML, and Home Assistant calls into Lock Code Manager at render time to produce the views, sections, and cards. The strategy reads your LCM config entries directly, so it stays in sync as slots and locks are added or removed without you having to edit the dashboard.
4	
5	LCM ships **four** strategies, all under the `custom:lock-code-manager*` family:
6	
7	- [Dashboard strategy](#dashboard-strategy) — generates an entire dashboard.
8	- [View strategy](#view-strategy) — generates a single view inside a dashboard.
9	- [Slot section strategy](#slot-section-strategy) — generates a single slot card inside a `sections`-type view.
10	- [Lock section strategy](#lock-section-strategy) — generates a single lock-codes card inside a `sections`-type view.
11	
12	For the user-facing decision guide on which one to pick, see [[Add a UI for lock code management|Add-a-UI-for-lock-code-management]].
13	
14	---
15	
16	## Dashboard strategy
17	
18	**Type:** `custom:lock-code-manager`
19	
20	Generates a complete dashboard:
21	
22	- One view per LCM config entry (slot cards stacked, optionally followed by lock-codes cards).
23	- An optional **User Codes** view containing one lock-codes card per managed lock.
24	
25	```yaml
```

1	# Lock Code Manager
2	
3	Lock Code Manager is a Home Assistant integration that keeps PIN codes in sync
4	across one or more locks, even across different lock providers (e.g. Z-Wave and
5	Matter locks sharing the same codes). Define your codes once and Lock Code
6	Manager handles setting, clearing, and monitoring them on every lock.
7	
8	Are you just looking for a simple UI to manage your lock's PIN codes? LCM has
9	you covered. Are you interested in more advanced scheduling capabilities where
10	you can set rules for when PINs are active, or you manage e.g. an Airbnb and
11	need to regularly rotate PINs? LCM still has you covered.
12	
13	Features:
14	
15	- Synchronize PIN codes across multiple locks and providers
16	- Automatic sync — codes are set and cleared as needed, with retry and
17	  drift detection
18	- Condition entities control when a code is active:
19	  - `calendar` — active during events
20	  - `binary_sensor` / `switch` / `input_boolean` — active when on
21	  - `schedule` — active during scheduled times
22	- [Blueprints](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Blueprints)
23	  for advanced use cases like usage limiting, calendar-driven PINs, and more
24	- Dashboard cards for managing codes and viewing lock status
25	
26	Supported lock integrations:
27	
28	| Integration | Read PINs | Push Updates | Code Events | Notes |
29	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
30	| [Z-Wave][wiki-zwave] | Varies | ✅ | ✅ | Some locks mask PINs |
31	| [ZHA][wiki-zha] | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Drift detection fallback if lock lacks programming events |
32	| [Zigbee2MQTT][wiki-zigbee2mqtt] (MQTT)² | Varies | ✅ | ✅ | Same broker as Z2M; PIN support depends on lock |
33	| [Matter][wiki-matter] | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | PINs write-only per spec |
34	| [Schlage WiFi][wiki-schlage] | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | Cloud-based, PINs masked |
35	| [Akuvox][wiki-akuvox]¹ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | Local API, polling-based |
36	| [Virtual][wiki-virtual]¹ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | For testing only |
37	
38	¹ Custom integration required ([Local Akuvox][local-akuvox],
39	[hass-virtual][hass-virtual])
40	
41	² **Zigbee2MQTT (MQTT)** — Pair the lock in [Zigbee2MQTT][zigbee2mqtt] with PIN/user-code support for your firmware.
42	The **Code Events** column refers to PIN-used automations from Lock Code Manager’s event entity
43	(which slots were used to lock/unlock).
44	Zigbee2MQTT lock/unlock actions with user identification are mapped to code slot events for PIN-used automations.
45	Configure Home Assistant’s **MQTT** integration on the **same broker** Zigbee2MQTT uses.
46	The default Zigbee2MQTT base topic `zigbee2mqtt` matches what Lock Code Manager expects unless you customize topics
47	(`{base_topic}/{friendly_name}/set|get`).
48	During LCM setup, choose your `lock.*` entity from **MQTT**.
49	If you rename the device in HA, keep it aligned with the **friendly name** in Zigbee2MQTT.
50	
51	[zigbee2mqtt]: https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/
52	[wiki-akuvox]: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Akuvox-integration
53	[wiki-zigbee2mqtt]: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Zigbee2MQTT-integration
54	[wiki-matter]: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Matter-integration
55	[wiki-schlage]: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Schlage-integration
56	[wiki-virtual]: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Virtual-integration
57	[local-akuvox]: https://github.com/pjaudiomv/hass-local-akuvox
58	[hass-virtual]: https://github.com/twrecked/hass-virtual
59	[wiki-zha]: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/ZHA-integration
60	[wiki-zwave]: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Z-Wave-integration
61	
62	Adding support for new lock integrations is straightforward — see the
63	[Adding a Provider](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Adding-a-Provider)
64	guide. Contributors welcome!
65	
66	## Integrations That Cannot Currently Be Supported
67	
68	Some lock integrations cannot currently be supported due to limitations in their underlying
69	libraries. See the [wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Unsupported-Integrations)
70	for details.
71	
72	## Condition Entity Integrations Not Supported
73	
74	Some condition entity integrations are not compatible. See the
75	[wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Unsupported-Condition-Entity-Integrations)
76	for details.
77	
78	## Installation
79	
80	The best way to install this integration is via HACS.
81	
82	1. Set up your locks in Home Assistant through a supported integration
83	   (Z-Wave, ZHA, Matter, Schlage, Zigbee2MQTT/MQTT, etc.)
84	2. Add this repository as a custom integration repository in HACS
85	3. Go to Settings > Devices & Services > Add Integration
86	4. Select Lock Code Manager
87	5. Follow the prompts - additional information about the configuration options are
88	   available in the Wiki
89	
90	## Blueprints
91	
92	Pre-built automations and templates for common lock management
93	patterns. See [BLUEPRINTS.md](BLUEPRINTS.md) for full details,
94	input tables, and import buttons.
95	
96	### Template blueprints
97	
98	- **Calendar Condition** — Binary sensor for calendar-based slot access
99	- **Date Range Condition** — Binary sensor for start/end date access
100	
101	### Automation blueprints
102	
103	- **Slot Usage Limiter** — Disable a slot after a set number of uses
104	- **Calendar PIN Setter** — Extract and set PINs from calendar events
105	- **Auto Re-lock** — Re-lock after a delay with day/night support
106	- **Lock on Door Close** — Lock when a door sensor detects closure
107	- **Slot Usage Notifier** — Notify when a code slot PIN is used
108	- **Condition Linker** — Assign a condition entity to a slot via UI
109	
110	## Learn More
111	
112	Visit the [Wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki) for detailed
113	documentation including configuration, troubleshooting, dashboard setup, and development guides.
114	
115	## UI & Dashboards
116	
117	Lock Code Manager provides Lovelace strategies and custom cards for managing PINs.
118	See the [wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Add-a-UI-for-lock-code-management)
119	for configuration options and setup guidance.
120	
121	## Inspiration
122	
123	I am a [keymaster](https://github.com/FutureTense/keymaster) maintainer,
124	and what I learned working on it, and the regular complaints users had about it generating
125	too many automations, entities, etc. led me to take a different approach. This isn't a
126	knock on `keymaster`, unfortunately a lot of what is built in this integration wasn't
127	possible for most of `keymaster`'s life. I briefly considered implementing this into
128	`keymaster` but:
129	
130	1. `keymaster` is still a great solution that works as is.
131	2. `keymaster` is surprisingly simple under the hood because it makes Home Assistant do a
132	   lot of the heavy lifting for figuring out when to enable and disable a usercode. This
133	   integration, on the other hand, attempts to do all of the heavy lifting internally in
134	   code, which means it will generate less entities and automations but it is likely more
135	   fragile to changes in HA Core or even changes in the codebase.
136	3. It would be impossible to seamlessly migrate users from the current implementation of
137	   `keymaster` to this integration's implementation. Rewriting `keymaster` to do this
138	   would have been the equivalent of creating a new integration anyway.
139	
140	## Thanks
141	
142	A big thank you to the other `keymaster` maintainers:
143	
144	- @FutureTense
145	- @firstof9
146	
147	As well as the person who created the base concept that `keymaster` evolved from:
148	@ptdalen
149

> AGENT

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
The current chip layout uses `flex: 1` on `.slot-name-row` and `justify-content: space-between` on `.slot-content-row` to get a one-line "name fills space, code stays right" arrangement. To stack vertically, both of those become unnecessary — switch the parent to `flex-direction: column` and the children naturally take full width with `min-width: 0` still doing the ellipsis-fallback work. Tests only assert on the `slot-name-pending-icon` class (not the layout classes), so this is a pure visual change with no test surface impact.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────

> AGENT

PR #1122 is open: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1122

**What changed (CSS-only):**
- `.slot-content-row` switched from horizontal flex (`align-items: center; justify-content: space-between`) to vertical flex (`flex-direction: column; gap: 4px`). The name now occupies row 1 with the full chip width; the PIN row sits below with the eye icon right-anchored as before.
- `.slot-name` dropped from `font-weight: 500` → `400` and `15px` → `14px`. The styles comment now explicitly documents the deliberate divergence from the slot card so future maintainers don't try to re-unify them.
- Dropped the now-redundant `.slot-content-row .slot-name-row { flex: 1 }` rule — the column layout makes it superfluous.

**Verification:** 148/148 lock-codes-card tests pass, `yarn build` clean, prek clean. Pure CSS change — no test assertions touch the layout classes I edited (only `slot-name-pending-icon`, which is preserved). I haven't browser-verified live (no dev server in this session), so please eyeball before merging — especially that the chip height on the empty-slot variant (where there's no PIN row, just a dash) still looks proportionate next to the populated chips.

name: project-test-refactor
description: Test refactor plan - rewrite tests from scratch following HA zwave_js patterns
type: project

Rewriting tests from scratch (not patching existing). Branch: `refactor/test-setup-fixtures` (already created off main at commit 3800c74).

**Why:** Current tests manually set `hass.data[DOMAIN]`, bypass `async_setup`, and create mock objects instead of going through real setup. This broke when `instance_id` was added to `async_setup`.

**Design principles (from user):**
- Start fresh, same file structure
- E2E design: every test goes through real `async_setup` / `async_setup_entry`
- Unit tests that are effectively integration tests (test through real code paths)
- Parametrize heavily
- Mock as far upstream as possible, not internal state
- No manual `hass.data` manipulation

**Reference architecture:**
- `/Users/raman/projects/home-assistant/tests/components/zwave_js/` — 1494-line conftest, JSON fixtures, package-scope state loading, function-scope models, `integration` fixture for real setup
- `/Users/raman/projects/zwave-js-server-python/tests/` — session-scope state, function-scope models, MockCommandProtocol

**Files to rewrite:**
- `test_helpers.py` — 7 places manually setting `hass.data[DOMAIN]` (worst offender)
- `test_init.py` — `test_resource_unload_skips_yaml_mode` broken by instance_id change
- `test_base.py` (providers) — creates BaseLock manually without integration setup
- `conftest.py` — needs expanded fixture hierarchy

**Pre-existing failure:** `test_resource_unload_skips_yaml_mode` fails because `instance_id.async_get(hass)` in `async_setup` writes to storage, affecting the test's caplog assertions.

> AGENT

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
The empty `slot-name-row` made sense in the old horizontal layout — it gave the row's flex child a left-side placeholder so the PIN's right-align stayed visually consistent across named/unnamed chips. In a column layout that placeholder becomes a *blank line above* the PIN, which is exactly what Copilot caught. This is a classic case where a layout switch invalidates a defensive empty-element pattern that was load-bearing under the old layout.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────

> AGENT

**Copilot's comment:** when `showName` is `false`, `_renderSlotChip` was emitting an empty `<span class="slot-name-row"></span>` as a fallback. In the old horizontal layout that worked as a left-side flex placeholder; in the new column layout it produces a blank row above the PIN on unnamed unmanaged chips.

**Fix (commit `9f5a3cd6`, pushed):** replaced the empty span with `nothing` so the row simply doesn't render in that case. `showName` is only false when the slot is *both* unnamed *and* explicitly unmanaged — exactly the case the empty placeholder was masking. All 148 lock-codes-card tests still pass; replied to the Copilot thread on the PR.

Want me to push the updated bundle to your HA instance and restart Core again so you can verify the unnamed-unmanaged chip looks right too?
